Stated Claim / Post Context:
Georgia court dismisses lawsuit seeking to block Fulton County absentee ballot drop-off policy

A Georgia judge Thursday dismissed a lawsuit that sought to block a Fulton County absentee ballot drop-off policy.

Actual Article Body:
By Natalie Note

October 1, 2026

A Georgia judge Thursday dismissed an anti-voting lawsuit challenging a Fulton County Board of Registration and Elections’ policy that increased the number of sites where voters could drop off absentee ballots in Georgia’s most populous county.

Superior Court Judge Scott McAfee granted members of the board’s motion to dismiss because the policy had been discontinued in May.

The Republican National Committee, the Fulton County Republican Party and Georgia secretary of state candidate Tim Fleming initially filed the lawsuit in June, seeking to prohibit the board from implementing or enforcing the policy.

“The Court concludes it lacks jurisdiction because the challenged policy is no longer in effect. The petition must therefore be dismissed as moot,” McAfee wrote.
